thread:
priya: Customer (Acme Fin) reporting intermittent 403 after service key rotation. Saw org header flip between requests. ReqIDs: 2169870001, 2169870025. Error in their logs: `signature_mismatch`. Any quick repro steps?
laura: Can you paste a sample curl they used and the exact response headers we saw? Which project header did they send?
priya: Their curl: 
```bash
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer svc-XYZ' \
  -H 'X-Redwood-Org: org-acme' \
  -H 'X-Redwood-Project: proj-prod' \
  -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
Support logs show req ids 2169870001 and 2169870025. Log snippet: `sig_verifier: signature_mismatch (expected alg RS256)`.
sam: SRE Q: can the customer run curl with an explicit `X-Request-Id` header and paste full `curl -v` output including response headers? Also capture Date and Content-Length from the response headers.
priya: They replied with response headers for req 2169870025: `x-rw-request-id: 2169870025`, `x-rw-verified-org: org-acme`, `x-rw-auth-status: denied`, and a `warning: signature mismatch`. They said they recently toggled an internal proxy that sometimes rewrites headers. Sending debug bundle after enabling verbose logs.
laura: Sounds like proxy is rewriting `X-Redwood-Project` or `Authorization`. @eng_ops_bot can you pull traces for 2169870001 and 2169870025 across edge->auth?
eng_ops_bot: Tracing: path edge-prod -> auth-proxy-1 -> router-2 -> inference. For req 2169870001, auth-proxy-1 rewrote `x-redwood-project` from `proj-prod` to `proj-staging` at 2026-03-15T15:12:03Z. Trace id: trace-789. No other config changes in our control plane at that exact second.
sam: If proxy rewrites project header, token scope can mismatch and lead to verified signature failure (token signed for proj-prod, seen as proj-staging). Repro checklist for customer: 1) run curl with exact header order including `-H 'X-Request-Id: <id>'`; 2) run with `--resolve` to hit origin bypassing CDN; 3) capture tcpdump on client side if possible. Priya, ask them to paste the raw `curl -v` outputs.
priya: They ran curl bypassing CDN and got 200 for req 2169871000. When routed through their proxy they get 403. They'll attach debug bundle and tcpdump.
laura: Good — confirms header rewrite in transit. Next steps: tell them to preserve `Authorization` and `X-Redwood-*` in proxy rules or use a forwarding header. Ops, we should add a quick playbook note and escalate to the vendor if the proxy is managed externally.
support-ian: Drafting minimal reproducer to send to customer. Proposed repro curl: 
```bash
curl -v https://edge.example.com/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer svc-ROTATED' \
  -H 'X-Redwood-Org: org-acme' \
  -H 'X-Redwood-Project: proj-prod' \
  -H 'X-Request-Id: repro-001' \
  --data '{"prompt":"test"}'
```
Run both directly (bypass proxy) and via proxy, attach both `curl -v` outputs + tcpdump + auth logs for those request ids. Also include any proxy rules that might normalize headers.
priya: :thumbsup: I'll send repro steps to customer. They also asked about billing — some retries may have caused duplicate token consumption. Can finance help?
laura: @support-ian FYI finance: if retries were caused by 4xx on our side (or by header normalization mid-flight) we will consider refunding token usage. Collect retried request ids and timestamps in the debug bundle.
eng_ops_bot: Deploy-bot note: vendor reported a failover event at 2026-03-15T15:11:00Z that triggered header normalization on auth-proxy-1. No config deploys from our side in the 15:10-15:20 window.
sam: We'll add a temporary rule to reject header rewriting at auth-proxy-1 and follow up with vendor. Priya, once you drop the debug bundle here (curl outputs + tcpdump + auth logs and proxy rules) we'll triage and coordinate a billing adjustment if warranted.
